sentences.text: From 2000 to 2025, days with a feels-like high of 90°F or more averaged 23.9 a year in the 2000s, 33.8 in the 2010s and 34.7 from 2020 to 2025, but the record shows no clear trend yet.
Days with a feels-like high of 100°F or more and days with 1 inch of rain or more also show no clear trend yet.
Climate models project days at or above 90°F air temperature: for 2041 to 2050 the middle model has 22.4 days a year, and the 7 models range from 11.6 to 31.1.
For 2001 to 2020 the middle model has 10 days a year and the models range from 5.2 to 13.8, so the models disagree on how many hot days to expect.
These are projections for a typical year in 2041 to 2050, on a grid about 25 km wide, and are not a forecast of any single year.
The models follow a high-emissions path, and a trend in the past record is reported only when a statistical test gives p under 0.05, so 26 years may simply be too few to tell.

past-hot-days.title: Days with a feels-like high of 90°F or more
past-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo historical weather archive (ERA5 reanalysis), daily, 2000 to 2025. Counted from the daily record at this address.
past-hot-days.text: Days with a feels-like high of 90°F or more, 2000 to 2025. 2000s: 23.9 days a year on average (239 days in 10 years); 2010s: 33.8 days a year on average (338 days in 10 years); 2020 to 2025: 34.7 days a year on average (208 days in 6 years). Trend test (Mann-Kendall with Sen slope, one value per year; a trend counts only if p is under 0.05). Result: no clear trend yet.

future-hot-days.title: Days per year with an air-temperature high of 90°F or more, in climate models
future-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API (CMIP6 HighResMIP models), daily temperature_2m_max. 7 of 7 CMIP6 HighResMIP models had data for this point.
future-hot-days.text: Average days a year at or above 90°F (air temperature, not feels-like) in the climate models, 7 models. 2001 to 2020: the middle model has 10 days a year; models range from 5.2 to 13.8. 2041 to 2050: the middle model has 22.4 days a year; models range from 11.6 to 31.1. The middle model changes by 12.4 days a year between the two periods. For comparison, the weather archive counted an average of 2.1 days a year at or above 90°F over 2001 to 2020.

caveat.title: What the projections are, and are not
caveat.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API; CMIP6 HighResMIP climate models
caveat.text: Climate-model projections (CMIP6), not a forecast; ~25 km grid; models disagree, so we show the range. These models follow a high-emissions path (as close to RCP8.5 as CMIP6 gets), and Open-Meteo adjusts them to match the past record at this spot, which does not change the size of the warming they show. They describe how often hot days could occur in a typical year of 2041 to 2050, not what any single year or day will do. A trend in the past record is reported only when a statistical test gives p under 0.05; otherwise the record says "no clear trend yet", which means the 26 years are too few or too variable to tell.
